_README: Deployment presets for liveClassifierTorchROS.py. This file is COMMITTED TO GIT so a
deployment site picks up new models and operating points with a plain `git pull` --
no environment variables to set on-site.
The FIRST entry of "configurations" is the one used at startup. To switch, either
reorder the list (and commit) or pass the preset name as an argument:
ros2 run magician_vision_classifier liveClassifierTorchROS --config low_false_alarm
The model's .pth/.json are auto-downloaded on first run from
http://ammar.gr/magician/models/CameraV2Models/ (ModelDownload.ensure_model), the same
directory scripts/uploadModels.sh pushes to.
gate.threshold semantics depend on gate.mode. Under the default "defect_mass" it
thresholds 1 - P(clean) -- the total probability mass on ANY defect class -- NOT the
max softmax probability. A max_prob threshold of the same number means something
completely different. Thresholds are NOT portable between models: re-read them from
that model's <name>_threshold_curve.json.
Every number under "measured" is read from the named threshold-curve file, not
estimated. They come from the run's held-out split, which was ALSO used to select the
checkpoint, so treat the absolute values as slightly optimistic -- the ranking between
operating points is sound (see ISSUES.md M3).
runtime.step / runtime.target_fps are the existing node defaults and are NOT tuned per
model: no throughput has been measured for these models yet (perf.csv has no rows for
them). Run benchmarkAllModels.py before trusting them on new hardware.

_comment: Measured operating curve for the default model, so an operator can pick a gate
level without opening the curve file. Read verbatim from
detected = fraction of DEFECT tiles flagged. false_alarm = fraction of CLEAN tiles
flagged; multiply by the tiles-per-frame count to get crosses per frame.
NOTE the curve is unusually FLAT: 0.30 -> 0.96 cuts false alarms 21x (10.27% ->
0.49%) for only 6 points of detection. High thresholds are cheap on this model.
This is model-specific -- on allclass_forthalt_custom the same move costs 15 points.
A false-alarm rate below ~0.15% is NOT reachable: the sweep stops at 0.995.

configurations.name: default
configurations.description: mix_convnext_tiny at the node's historical gate setting. Best detection-vs-false-alarm of the mix_* family: 92.7% of defect tiles caught for 0.88% false alarms on clean tiles.

configurations.name: low_false_alarm
configurations.description: Same model at its trainer-computed deployment point (highest detection subject to a 0.5% false-alarm budget). Roughly halves false alarms for 1.6 points of detection.

configurations.name: minimal_false_alarm
configurations.description: Strictest useful gate: 0.22% false alarms, still catching 88.3% of defect tiles. Use when crosses are acted on automatically and a false stop is expensive. Below roughly 0.15% FA is not reachable on this model.

configurations.name: one_percent_fa
configurations.description: Highest detection available inside a 1% false-alarm budget. Practically the same detection as the default (92.9% vs 92.7%) at a marginally higher false-alarm rate -- pick whichever budget the line actually enforces.

configurations.name: high_recall
configurations.description: mix_convnext_tiny at its KPI-optimal gate (misses weighted 2x against false alarms). Use only where an operator reviews the crosses -- the false-alarm rate is an order of magnitude higher than the default.

configurations.name: lightweight
configurations.description: mix_shufflenet_v2_x1_0 -- by far the smallest archive (14 MB vs 311 MB) for constrained hardware or slow links. Detection is materially worse at a matched false-alarm budget, so prefer the default unless throughput or download size forces this.
